pipeline_name: Srednevilyuyskoye Gas Condensate Field-Yakutsk Gas Pipeline

validity.recommendation: No structural fix needed. Existence, routing and classification are solidly corroborated; see the two separate spec flags below (StartYear1 and Capacity attribution).
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, well-documented line, not a GEM-only entity. Multiple independent sources describe this exact 530mm 'String I' of the SVGKM-Mastakh-Berge-Yakutsk system: neftegaz.ru's field/infrastructure reference page (671733), neftegaz.ru's 2019 explosion/repair article (194257, describing this exact section rupturing near Kysyl-Syr), ipng.ysn.ru's 2021 parliamentary-panel article (84km Kysyl-Syr-Mastakh figure), and (via Wayback, live URL is a JS anti-bot shell) interfax-russia.ru's Rostekhnadzor-violations article and State Duma funding article, both naming Sakhatransneftegaz JSC as operator of the Kysyl-Syr-Mastakh corridor. CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are correct -- neftegaz.ru explicitly calls the system a 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk/transmission gas pipeline) and the Rostekhnadzor article treats it as a regulated trunk asset. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 32-row roster, specifically the 8-row Sakhatransneftegaz family: this system is built as 2 parallel 530mm lines ('нитки') on the Kysyl-Syr-Mastakh-Berge-Yakutsk corridor plus a later 3rd, 720mm line. P3365 is explicitly 'String I' of the Kysyl-Syr-Mastakh segment; a 'String II' sibling on the same segment and a separate 720mm 'String III' sibling (matching P6694's spec almost exactly, see cross_row_leads) are DIFFERENT physical pipes, not a mislabeled duplicate of P3365. No relabel/segment-double-count risk found for P3365 itself, though see the Capacity flag below for a related attribution risk shared with its 530mm sibling.

validity.recommendation: Recommend changing StartYear1 from 2014 to 1967 for this 530mm 'String I' row. 2014 is well-documented elsewhere in this GEM family as the commissioning year of the separate, newer 720mm THIRD line (matching sibling P6694's own recorded StartYear=2014 almost exactly) -- suggesting the sheet may have copied the 3rd-line date onto this older 530mm string in error. Do not apply without a second independent (non-neftegaz.ru) confirmation of 1967 specifically for the KYSYL-SYR-MASTAKH segment (as opposed to the system generally); flagging as a concern rather than auto-correcting given the single-outlet sourcing.
validity.researcher_notes: Two neftegaz.ru pages (same outlet, so NOT counted as fully independent) both state the SYSTEM's two 530mm lines were commissioned in 1967: the field reference page (671733) says 'Диаметр трубы - 530 мм. Ввод в эксплуатацию - с 1967 года (МГП Таас Тумус - Якутск)... Эксплуатируется с 1967 года (с момента ввода в эксплуатацию первого магистрального газопровода Таас Тумус - Якутск)'; the 2019 explosion article (194257) states explicitly: '2 нитки МГП имеют Ø 530 мм, 3-я нитка, введенная в эксплуатацию в конце 2014 г. - Ø 720 мм' (the two 530mm lines vs. the 3rd 720mm line commissioned at the END of 2014) -- i.e. this same article's OWN text draws the 1967-vs-2014 distinction that GEM's sheet appears to have collapsed. Sibling ProjectID P6694 ('Mastakh-Yakutsk III', 720mm/384km per roster) matches this 3rd line's spec (720mm, 384km, ~8 million m3/day, commissioned late 2014) almost exactly -- see cross_row_leads. Separately, the interfax-russia.ru State Duma article (read via Wayback) discusses a 2018 rupture on the FIRST line ('первая нитка') that was serving as emergency backup while the (then-unfinished) third line was still under construction -- independent corroboration (a different outlet, interfax vs. neftegaz) that a 'first line' already existed and was in active service well before 2014, consistent with an 1967-era commissioning and inconsistent with StartYear1=2014. This satisfies partial independence (interfax corroborates PRE-2014 existence of a first line, though not the specific year 1967), so this is filed as a medium/high-value spec concern rather than UNRESOLVED, but a second source stating '1967' specifically for the Kysyl-Syr-Mastakh segment (as opposed to the system as a whole, or the Taas-Tumus-Yakutsk line specifically as in sibling P2334's shard) was not found this run.

validity.recommendation: Keep Capacity=1.50 bcm/y as recorded for now (it is within rounding of the source figure once converted), but flag that the source states this design capacity for the TWO 530mm lines COMBINED, not per-string -- so if a separate 'String II' sibling row also carries 1.50 bcm/y, one or both may be double-counting a system-level aggregate onto a single-segment cell. No corrected per-string split figure is available to propose.
validity.researcher_notes: The existing_ref_checks flagged this as a content false-negative (substring '1.5'/'1.50' absent) -- correctly a false negative, not a real miss: the neftegaz.ru explosion article (194257) states 'Проектная производительность 2 х ниток - 4,2 млн м3/сутки, максимальная - 6,3 млн м3/сутки' (design capacity of the 2 [530mm] lines - 4.2 million m3/day, maximum 6.3 million m3/day). Converting: 4.2 million m3/day x 365 = 1,533 million m3/y = ~1.53 bcm/y, matching the recorded 1.50 bcm/y within rounding -- BUT the Russian phrasing most naturally reads as the COMBINED capacity of BOTH 530mm strings together, not a per-line figure. This is the classic aggregate-vs-segment trap: if GEM's separate 'String II' sibling row for this same Kysyl-Syr-Mastakh segment also independently carries Capacity=1.50 bcm/y, then the SAME system-level total is being attributed to each string individually rather than being split between them. I could not find a source giving the two strings' capacities separately, so no corrected number is proposed -- flagging the ambiguity for the record.

summary: P3365 (Srednevilyuyskoye GCF-Yakutsk Gas Pipeline, Kysyl-Syr-Mastakh String I segment) is real, correctly classified (Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission), and confirmed distinct from its 720mm String III sibling (a strong match to P6694, filed as a cross_row_lead) -- no duplicate/relabel risk found for P3365 itself. All 15 worklist units carry a fills[] record: REFS_ADDED/REVERIFIED for Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Capacity (1.50 bcm/y, confirmed within rounding but flagged for possible system-aggregate double-counting), Length (84km), Diameter (530mm), FuelSource, Location, Operator, and Owner; UNRESOLVED with documented search trails for Proposal, Construction, Pressure, and SegmentCost (no source found). Staged 3 validity concerns: (1) a confirmed-with-caveats existence/classification finding (none, informational); (2) a SPEC concern recommending StartYear1 be corrected from the recorded 2014 to 1967 -- both neftegaz.ru sources describe this exact segment's 530mm lines as 1967-commissioned, with 2014 belonging only to a separate, newer 720mm third line (matching sibling P6694), suggesting a likely cross-row date misattribution; independence is partial (interfax-russia.ru corroborates pre-2014 existence of a 'first line' but not the specific year 1967), so flagged as medium-tier rather than auto-corrected; (3) a SPEC concern on Capacity: the sourced 4.2 million m3/day figure is stated as the COMBINED design capacity of BOTH 530mm strings, not per-line, raising a possible aggregate-attributed-to-segment risk if a 'String II' sibling also independently carries 1.50 bcm/y. status_reviews verdict: confirm (operating), evidence current as of Dec 2025. Three cross_row_leads filed: P6694 (the 720mm third line spec match, also explaining the StartYear1 mixup), P3361 (a well-documented Dec 2024 new-line launch on this same corridor), and an unidentified 'Kysyl-Syr-Mastakh II' sibling that should be checked for the same Capacity aggregation risk. UNRESOLVED: Proposal, Construction, Pressure, SegmentCost.
